statement.p: Let y = \sqrt[3]{x} (x^{3}+x^{6}) Calculate the derivative using the product rule.
(It doesn't matter which part of the sum you enter first or second.)
Try checking your answer by multiplying y out and then using power rule.

hint.p: y is a product of two functions, \displaystyle x^{\left({\frac{1}{3}}\right)} and x^{3}+x^{6}.

solution.p: The function y= is a product of two functions, say f(x)= x^{\left({\frac{1}{3}}\right)} and g(x)=x^{3}+x^{6}. Then taking the derivatives we get f'(x)=\left({\frac{1}{3}}\right)\frac{1}{x^{0.666667}} and g'(x)=3x^{2}+6x^{5}. Finally, the product rule says that \left[f(x)g(x)\right]'=f'(x)g(x)+g'(x)f(x) so y'= (\left({\frac{1}{3}}\right)\frac{1}{x^{0.666667}}) \cdot (x^{3}+x^{6}) + (3x^{2}+6x^{5})\cdot (x^{\left({\frac{1}{3}}\right)}).
